title: Coherence of evaluation transposes under strong monoidal functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be symmetric monoidal closed categories [def-nagata-category] and [def-sfb-monoidal-category], with tensor $\otimes$, internal Hom $H$, and natural adjunction bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(T,H(K,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes K,M)$ whose counits are $\mathrm{ev}$. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be strong monoidal [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] and compatible with the symmetries, with coherent natural isomorphisms $t_{U,V}:FU\otimes FV\xrightarrow{\sim}F(U\otimes V)$ and a unit isomorphism. For every $K,M$ let $v^F_{K,M}:FH_{\mathcal C}(K,M)\to H_{\mathcal D}(FK,FM)$ be the transpose of $F(\mathrm{ev})\circ t_{H(K,M),K}$. Then this map is the unique arrow satisfying
$$\mathrm{ev}_{FK,FM}\circ(v^F_{K,M}\otimes1)=F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ t_{H(K,M),K}.$$
It is natural contravariantly in $K$ and covariantly in $M$. If $a:T\otimes K\to M$ has transpose $a^\sharp$, then $v^F_{K,M}\circ F(a^\sharp)$ is the transpose of $F(a)\circ t_{T,K}$.

Write $\mu:H(M,N)\otimes H(K,M)\to H(K,N)$ for composition characterized by two successive evaluations. For every triple one has
$$v^F_{K,N}\circ F(\mu_{\mathcal C})\circ t_{H(M,N),H(K,M)}=\mu_{\mathcal D}\circ(v^F_{M,N}\otimes v^F_{K,M}).$$
For another symmetric monoidal closed category $\mathcal E$, strong symmetric monoidal functors $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$, $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$, and a monoidal natural isomorphism $h:GF\xrightarrow{\sim}J$, the corresponding comparisons satisfy
$$v^J_{K,M}\circ h_{H(K,M)}=H_{\mathcal E}(h_K^{-1},h_M)\circ v^G_{FK,FM}\circ G(v^F_{K,M}).$$
For the identity functor with its canonical monoidal structure, $v^{\mathrm{id}}_{K,M}=1$. These identities do not require any $v$ to be invertible; tensor and functor associators are the specified coherent ones.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 4; returned proof steps 10, 11, 12; extracted argument preserved verbatim in Q07 report, not a new literature theorem

proof.text:
Write $\Theta_{T,K,M}$ for the stipulated natural adjunction bijection and $U_{T,K,M}=\Theta_{T,K,M}^{-1}$. In either category, naturality in $T$ applied to $1_{H(K,M)}$ gives $U(q)=\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}\circ(q\otimes1_K)$. Since $U$ is a bijection it detects equality. More generally its naturality says
$$U(H(a,b)\circ q\circ r)=b\circ U(q)\circ(r\otimes a)$$
for $a:K'\to K$, $b:M\to M'$, $r:T'\to T$, and $q:T\to H(K,M)$. Indeed apply $\Theta$ to the right side: naturality gives $H(a,b)\circ\Theta(U(q))\circ r=H(a,b)\circ q\circ r$, and cancel $\Theta$. These are consequences of the assumed natural bijections, with the tensor bifunctor and composition conventions of [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and [def-nagata-category].

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text: Put $V=H_{\mathcal C}(K,M)$ and $e^F_{K,M}=F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ t^F_{V,K}$. By definition $v^F_{K,M}=\Theta(e^F_{K,M})$, so $U(v^F_{K,M})=e^F_{K,M}$. The evaluation formula from step 1 is exactly the claimed equation. Conversely any arrow satisfying that equation has uncurrying $e^F_{K,M}$ and therefore equals $\Theta(e^F_{K,M})$. This proves existence and uniqueness without an invertibility assumption on $v$. The tensorator has the direction specified in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor].

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text:
For $a:T\otimes K\to M$, put $a^\sharp=\Theta(a)$, so $\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}\circ(a^\sharp\otimes1_K)=a$. Naturality of the tensorator in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] and step 2 give
$$U(v^F_{K,M}\circ F(a^\sharp))=F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ t^F_{V,K}\circ(F(a^\sharp)\otimes1_{FK})=F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}\circ(a^\sharp\otimes1_K))\circ t^F_{T,K}=F(a)\circ t^F_{T,K}.$$
Apply $\Theta$ to obtain the required compatibility with transposition.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text:
For $b:M\to M'$, let $V'=H_{\mathcal C}(K,M')$. Naturality in step 1 gives $\mathrm{ev}_{K,M'}\circ(H(1_K,b)\otimes1_K)=b\circ\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}$. Thus tensorator naturality [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] gives
$$U(v^F_{K,M'}\circ F H(1_K,b))=F(b\circ\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ t^F_{V,K}=F(b)\circ e^F_{K,M}=U(H(1_{FK},Fb)\circ v^F_{K,M}).$$
Injectivity of $U$ proves covariant naturality in $M$.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text:
For $a:K'\to K$, step 1 applied to evaluation gives $\mathrm{ev}_{K',M}\circ(H(a,1_M)\otimes1_{K'})=\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}\circ(1_V\otimes a)$. Consequently, by tensorator naturality [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor],
$$U(v^F_{K',M}\circ F H(a,1_M))=F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}\circ(1_V\otimes a))\circ t^F_{V,K'}=e^F_{K,M}\circ(1_{FV}\otimes Fa)=U(H(Fa,1_{FM})\circ v^F_{K,M}).$$
Cancel $U$. Composing this identity with step 4, and using bifunctoriality of $H$, proves simultaneous contravariant/covariant naturality.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text:
For composition put $A=H_{\mathcal C}(M,N)$ and $B=H_{\mathcal C}(K,M)$. The definition of $\mu_{\mathcal C}$ in the statement is precisely
$$\mathrm{ev}_{K,N}\circ(\mu_{\mathcal C}\otimes1_K)=\mathrm{ev}_{M,N}\circ(1_A\otimes\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{A,B,K}.$$
It uniquely defines $\mu_{\mathcal C}$ by $\Theta$; the same formula defines $\mu_{\mathcal D}$. Define $s^F=t^F_{A\otimes B,K}\circ(t^F_{A,B}\otimes1_{FK})$. Its source is $(FA\otimes FB)\otimes FK$ and target $F((A\otimes B)\otimes K)$. The associativity axiom in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] is exactly
$$F(\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{A,B,K})\circ s^F=t^F_{A,B\otimes K}\circ(1_{FA}\otimes t^F_{B,K})\circ\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{FA,FB,FK}.$$
Thus no suppression of associators or general coherence theorem is needed.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text:
Let $L=v^F_{K,N}\circ F(\mu_{\mathcal C})\circ t^F_{A,B}$. Uncurrying, step 2 and naturality of $t^F$ with respect to $\mu_{\mathcal C}$ in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] give
$$U(L)=F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,N})\circ t^F_{H(K,N),K}\circ(F(\mu_{\mathcal C})\otimes1)\circ(t^F_{A,B}\otimes1)=F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,N}\circ(\mu_{\mathcal C}\otimes1_K))\circ s^F.$$
By step 6 this equals $F(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N}\circ(1_A\otimes\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{A,B,K})\circ s^F$.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text:
Let $R=\mu_{\mathcal D}\circ(v^F_{M,N}\otimes v^F_{K,M})$. Expand $U(R)$ using the defining equation for $\mu_{\mathcal D}$ from step 6. Naturality of $\alpha^{\mathcal D}$ [def-sfb-monoidal-category], followed by the two evaluation equations from step 2, gives
$$U(R)=F(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})\circ t^F_{A,M}\circ(1_{FA}\otimes F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}))\circ(1_{FA}\otimes t^F_{B,K})\circ\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{FA,FB,FK}.$$
Naturality of $t^F$ for $\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}:B\otimes K\to M$ rewrites $t^F_{A,M}\circ(1\otimes F(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}))$ as $F(1_A\otimes\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ t^F_{A,B\otimes K}$. Substitute the associativity equation of step 6 to obtain
$$U(R)=F(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N}\circ(1_A\otimes\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{A,B,K})\circ s^F=U(L).$$
Cancel $U$ to prove the internal-Hom composition identity. Only tensor bifunctoriality, the displayed naturality equations and the associativity axiom of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] were used.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text:
For the composite functor $P=GF$, its tensorator is $t^P_{X,Y}=G(t^F_{X,Y})\circ t^G_{FX,FY}$; this is the specified composite monoidal structure. Put $z=v^G_{FK,FM}\circ G(v^F_{K,M})$. Step 2 for $G$, naturality of $t^G$ [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], and then step 2 for $F$ give
$$U(z)=G(\mathrm{ev}_{FK,FM})\circ t^G_{H(FK,FM),FK}\circ(G(v^F_{K,M})\otimes1)=G(\mathrm{ev}_{FK,FM}\circ(v^F_{K,M}\otimes1))\circ t^G_{FV,FK}$$
$$=GF(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ G(t^F_{V,K})\circ t^G_{FV,FK}=P(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ t^P_{V,K}=U(v^P_{K,M}).$$
Therefore $z=v^P_{K,M}$ by injectivity. The calculation uses only the tensor maps of the given strong monoidal structures.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text:
Now let $h:P\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ be the stipulated monoidal natural isomorphism. Its monoidality means $t^J_{X,Y}\circ(h_X\otimes h_Y)=h_{X\otimes Y}\circ t^P_{X,Y}$. With $V=H_{\mathcal C}(K,M)$, naturality of $h$ at $\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}$ and step 2 give
$$U(v^J_{K,M}\circ h_V)\circ(1_{PV}\otimes h_K)=J(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ t^J_{V,K}\circ(h_V\otimes h_K)=h_M\circ P(\mathrm{ev}_{K,M})\circ t^P_{V,K}=h_M\circ U(v^P_{K,M}).$$
On the other hand step 1 gives
$$U(H(h_K^{-1},h_M)\circ v^P_{K,M})\circ(1_{PV}\otimes h_K)=h_M\circ U(v^P_{K,M})\circ(1_{PV}\otimes h_K^{-1})\circ(1_{PV}\otimes h_K)=h_M\circ U(v^P_{K,M}).$$
The tensor bifunctor of [def-sfb-monoidal-category] makes $1_{PV}\otimes h_K$ invertible, with inverse $1_{PV}\otimes h_K^{-1}$. Cancel this morphism and then $U$. Substitution of step 9 is the required formula for $h:GF\cong J$, with the stated variance and without inverting any $v$.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, associativity of tensor product and uniqueness of transpose; explicit formal calculation by Q127

proof.text: For the identity functor with its canonical monoidal structure, the tensorator $t^{\mathrm{id}}_{V,K}$ is the identity. Hence $U(v^{\mathrm{id}}_{K,M})=\mathrm{ev}_{K,M}=U(1_{H(K,M)})$ by steps 1 and 2. Cancel $U$ to obtain $v^{\mathrm{id}}_{K,M}=1$. Together with steps 3--5, 8 and 10 this proves all the clauses. No dualizability, rigidity, exactness, or invertibility of the internal-Hom comparisons was used.
